transcript.content:
You write Verilog practice problems for complete beginners and verify nothing yourself:
your output is checked by a simulator and by mutation testing, and any failure comes back to you.

Reply with ONE JSON object in a ```json code block and nothing else. Keys:
  "spec": plain-English problem statement, 50-150 words. Say what top_module must do and what
          each provided module does. Do NOT give the wiring: which bits go to which instance, what
          a carry-in or select is tied to, or how outputs are combined. Working that out is the
          exercise; the hints reveal it step by step. Never include code.
  "given_sv": Verilog source of every provided module, or "" if none.
  "ref_sv": "module RefModule(...)" with exactly the same ports as top_module, written
            behaviourally (for example with + and assign), never using the provided modules.
  "solution_sv": what a good learner submits: "module top_module(...)" built the intended way
                 (instantiating the provided modules), plus any module the learner must write.
  "directed": list of input assignments as integers, e.g. [{"a": 5, "b": 3}]. Cover the cases
              that expose the common mistakes (carries, sign bits, each select value).
  "hints": {"L0": one sentence naming the concept to think about,
            "L3": the wiring in words (which signals connect where), still no code}.
  "common_mistakes": 2-4 short descriptions of mistakes beginners make on this problem.

Rules: Verilog-2005 (logic is allowed). No system tasks ($display etc.), no `include, no initial
blocks in ref_sv or solution_sv. Clocked logic uses posedge clk. Port names and widths must match
the given top_module header exactly.

Problem id: module_add
Outline: Build a 32-bit adder from two provided 16-bit adders; the low half's carry feeds the high half and the final carry is dropped.
top_module header: module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum);
Provided module(s): module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout)
The solution must instantiate: 2 x add16
Directed vectors: Include vectors where the low half carries out, e.g. a = 32'h0000FFFF, b = 1.

```json
{
  "spec": "Build a 32-bit adder by connecting two 16-bit adders. The provided add16 module adds two 16-bit numbers with a carry-in and produces a 16-bit sum and a carry-out. The top_module must add two 32-bit numbers a and b by splitting them into low and high 16-bit halves. The carry-out from the low half adder becomes the carry-in for the high half adder. The final carry-out from the high half is discarded. The 32-bit sum is the concatenation of the high and low sums.",
  "given_sv": "module add16(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input cin, output [15:0] sum, output cout);\n  assign {cout, sum} = a + b + cin;\nendmodule",
  "ref_sv": "module RefModule(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum);\n  assign sum = a + b;\nendmodule",
  "solution_sv": "module top_module(input [31:0] a, input [31:0] b, output [31:0] sum);\n  wire [15:0] low_sum, high_sum;\n  wire low_cout, high_cout;\n  add16 low_adder (.a(a[15:0]), .b(b[15:0]), .cin(1'b0), .sum(low_sum), .cout(low_cout));\n  add16 high_adder (.a(a[31:16]), .b(b[31:16]), .cin(low_cout), .sum(high_sum), .cout(high_cout));\n  assign sum = {high_sum, low_sum};\nendmodule",
  "directed": [
    {"a": 0, "b": 0},
    {"a": 1, "b": 1},
    {"a": 65535, "b": 1},
    {"a": 4294967295, "b": 1},
    {"a": 2147483648, "b": 2147483648},
    {"a": 4294967295, "b": 4294967295}
  ],
  "hints": {
    "L0": "Think about how to split a 32-bit addition into two 16-bit additions with carry propagation.",
    "L3": "Connect the low 16 bits of a and b to the first add16 with carry-in 0; feed its carry-out into the second add16's carry-in along with the high 16 bits of a and b; combine the two 16-bit sums into the 32-bit output."
  },
  "common_mistakes": [
    "Forgetting to set the low adder's carry-in to 0.",
    "Swapping the high and low halves when concatenating the sum.",
    "Using the final carry-out as part of the sum.",
    "Not connecting the carry-out of the low adder to the carry-in of the high adder."
  ]
}
```
